title: Saidu Sharif I Stupa
subtitle: Buddhist stupa on the edge of Saidu Sharif, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Saidu Sharif I Stupa and Monastery
edits: The main stupa is the Atlas maquette (backend/tools/blender/stupa.py): the square base 19.6 m x 3.2 m, the first cylindrical body (tier) 13.4 m and the drum 13.1 m are measured from the MAIP restitution drawing's scale bar; only the surviving base is modelled, and its stair faces north as Wikipedia describes. The model is placed by the build at the ground of the place point.

The Terrace of the Stupas is a rectangular stone-paved floor 40 m east-west by 30 m north-south (estimated; no source gives its size), levelled by the build to the ground at the place point within 27 m, and drawn in grey stone slabs with joints (estimated pattern).
Its dressed-stone retaining edge, 1.0 m high and 0.8 m thick, is estimated from photo 3; its height and line are not surveyed.

Eight minor stupas on square stepped bases of 2 to 4 m, mostly ruined down to the base, three with a low drum, are estimated from photos 1 and 2; their number, positions, sizes and shades are illustrative.
The four corner columns of the MAIP restitution are not drawn: no photo shows them standing, and their heights are unsourced.

The monastery on the upper terrace is drawn inside the OSM footprint 'Saidu Sharif Monastery' (way 1078000527) as a walled courtyard, 24 m by 38 m, with six cells along each long side: cell sizes, wall heights and flat roofs are estimated. Its ground is the DEM, which is not levelled to a separate upper terrace (no source gives that height); the 30 m DEM cannot show the cut.
Trees within 92 m of the place point are left out, which covers the monastery footprint so it can be seen; WorldCover 2021 maps tree cover there.

The walking circle is a 36 m circle around the stupa terrace; it is not a mapped trail. The walk from the trailhead on Saidu Sharif Road to the stupa crosses the town ground on the easiest slope over the DEM.
